milestones.title: Working local film library and safe external adapter foundations
exit_criteria: Import existing clips, preserve originals, trim/label/review/retrieve them, manage playlists, and export audio-preserving MP4s through the local UI.
Qualify local API, persistence, provenance, and real FFmpeg behavior; verify installed-package assets.
Provide Kinovea handoff/sidecar preservation and CV suggestion import as explicit optional adapters. Real Windows execution and model inference remain separate later gates.

milestones.title: Faster film study and deeper Kinovea interoperability
exit_criteria: Support consistent/batch labeling, alternative cuts, accurate frame navigation, comparisons, annotations, and saved review sessions.
Validate versioned KVA interpretation and conflict-aware reconciliation without losing original sidecars.

milestones.title: Qualified optional football computer vision
exit_criteria: Establish a pinned external environment, reviewed calibration/pre-snap inputs, bounded jobs, and complete source-bound artifacts.
Render audio-preserving overlays, maintain correction/identity decisions, and evaluate representative owner-approved footage.
Calibration transfer and track-quality improvements remain explicit evidence-gated enhancements.

milestones.title: Desktop convenience, recovery, scale, and release confidence
exit_criteria: Qualify declared macOS/Windows installation paths and supported Kinovea versions.
Demonstrate full backup/restore, portable exports, migration/write-failure recovery, and safe derived-cache cleanup.
Record scale/media limits, dependency provenance, and final capability-specific release evidence. Independent recovery work can start immediately after M1.

sources.title: football-cv README and author-reported evaluation
sources.notes: Documentation describes alignment-derived position groups; evaluation is author-reported on private labels. Detector wording drifts from code.

sources.title: football-cv high-level analysis API
sources.notes: Explicit persistent data_dir and play_id are needed; default analysis uses a temporary directory.

sources.title: football-cv detector implementation
sources.notes: Selects RF-DETR when available, otherwise torchvision Faster R-CNN; dependency guard still checks ultralytics. MPS/CPU selection. Heavy model construction may obtain weights.

sources.title: football-cv overlay renderer
sources.notes: Frame-based MP4 rendering does not carry source audio into its output; wrapper must preserve media provenance and timing.

sources.title: football-cv local viewer server
sources.notes: Development viewer APIs for frames, calibration, analysis stages, and artifacts; not the application's production server.

sources.title: football-cv viewer landing page
sources.notes: Upload handler attaches a local object URL for playback and explicitly says analysis requires the backend.

sources.title: Kinovea official downloads, platform requirements, and license
sources.notes: Windows x86-64; official page excludes Apple Silicon support. GPL v2. External application only.

sources.title: Kinovea official reference manual
sources.notes: Describes playback, comparison, annotations, measurements, and exports. Older manual must be read with release notes.

sources.title: Kinovea 2023.1 release notes
sources.notes: Working-zone boundaries and import options can persist in annotations; time-origin alignment affects importing into different videos.

sources.title: Kinovea 2025.1 release notes
sources.notes: Documents -video2 comparison launch and multi-window behavior.

sources.title: Kinovea 2025.2 release notes
sources.notes: Includes timing and KVA loading fixes; release-specific integration fixtures are necessary.

tickets.title: Establish the local application and capability boundary
tickets.outcome: Start a private film room on one computer with actionable setup feedback and no automatic external processing.
scope: Create the Python package, CLI, same-origin static application, and FastAPI startup/shutdown lifecycle.
Load app-owned workspace configuration and expose health/capability information for FFmpeg, ffprobe, Kinovea, and optional football-cv.
non_goals: Public hosting, account management, provider uploads, automatic weight downloads, or native desktop installers.
acceptance_checks: A fresh configured data directory starts through the documented CLI and responds on loopback.
GET /api/health reports the application version and an explicit available/reason state for each optional capability.
Starting the app performs no film upload, model execution, or model download.
Startup and shutdown create/close the database and export worker without leaving duplicate workers.
risks: An optional missing executable must disable its dependent feature without hiding the rest of the library.
Do not confuse an importable Python dependency with a qualified native application or trained model.

tickets.title: Persist film records and immutable source provenance
tickets.outcome: Keep every review attached to the correct original film across application restarts.
scope: Create SQLite records for clips, games, players, tags, revisions, notes, playlists, jobs, and imported suggestions.
Assign opaque IDs and retain source SHA-256, duration, media properties, original filename, and application-owned storage location.
non_goals: Roster biometric identity resolution, cloud databases, or deducing a person's identity from a file hash.
acceptance_checks: Restarting the application preserves imported records and relationships.
Foreign-key enforcement rejects nonexistent game, player, or clip references.
SHA-256 and media properties cannot be changed through metadata edit routes.
Source-relative times remain stable when a view range or title changes.
Database files and media directories are ignored by git.
risks: A source hash identifies bytes; separate clips of the same player must never be merged by identity assumptions.
Multiple-source and multi-angle models may require later additive migrations.

tickets.title: Import existing clips safely with duplicate detection
tickets.outcome: Bring the owner's existing game clips into the library without damaging originals or multiplying identical imports.
scope: Accept bounded multipart video uploads and copy successful imports into managed storage.
Probe media, compute source hashes, create thumbnails where available, and report duplicates explicitly.
non_goals: Whole-game automatic play detection, remote video download, and importing arbitrary server filesystem paths.
acceptance_checks: A generated audio/video fixture imports with the correct duration, dimensions, audio flag, and source hash.
A second import of identical bytes returns the original clip ID and duplicate=true.
Unsupported, corrupt, oversized, and empty uploads return useful errors and leave no committed clip.
Client filenames containing traversal or shell characters cannot escape the managed workspace.
A failed probe or copy does not leave a valid-looking clip with missing source bytes.
risks: Content-type and file extension alone are not proof that a video can be decoded.
Source copying requires temporary space; failure cleanup must preserve existing clips.

tickets.title: Save metadata with optimistic concurrency and revision restore
tickets.outcome: Edit labels confidently and recover earlier review choices without silently losing another tab's changes.
scope: Update title, description, phase, review status, game, tags, player references, and selected range with a required version.
Persist revision snapshots and restore editable metadata as a new revision.
non_goals: Full undo of source files, automatic conflict merging, or removal of prior history.
acceptance_checks: A current-version PATCH increments version and records the previous/new review state consistently.
A stale-version PATCH returns 409 and leaves the stored clip unchanged.
Replacing tag/player lists validates and normalizes their inputs without partially applying invalid relationships.
Restoring a prior revision requires current_version and creates a new version rather than rewinding history.
Immutable source fields and invalid enum values are rejected.
risks: Whole-list replacement is deliberate; UI must preserve unsaved edits until success or an explicit conflict resolution.
A restored timestamp must still satisfy the immutable source duration.

tickets.title: Review source video with a non-destructive selected interval
tickets.outcome: Tighten each clip for future watching while keeping the complete source available.
scope: Support byte-range/HEAD source playback, selected in/out times, looping, and browser playback-speed controls.
Save 0 <= start_seconds < end_seconds <= source_duration as metadata.
non_goals: Guaranteed frame-accurate browser seeking, drawing tools, or deleting the original media outside the selected interval.
acceptance_checks: Valid byte-range requests return the expected bytes and invalid ranges return a controlled response.
A trim update never changes the source file hash or source_duration.
Invalid, reversed, non-finite, or out-of-bounds selections are rejected.
The UI can mark in/out, play or loop the saved interval, and reopen it after a restart.
All displayed/editable timestamps refer to the original source rather than a previously exported trim.
risks: Browser decoders may seek to nearby frames; exact frame navigation is a later qualification task.
Very tight trims can remove pre-snap alignment needed by later CV analysis.

tickets.title: Add durable timed coaching notes
tickets.outcome: Record what to watch and reopen the relevant moment without relying on filenames.
scope: Create/list/delete clip notes with optional source-relative timestamps.
Display note markers or links that seek the selected source to the stored moment.
non_goals: Audio dictation, collaborative comments, or editable Kinovea drawing objects.
acceptance_checks: An untimed note and a timed note survive restart and return against the correct clip.
A timed note accepts zero and source-duration boundaries according to the API contract, and rejects out-of-bounds/non-finite values.
Deleting a note from one clip cannot delete a note belonging to another clip.
A note containing HTML is displayed as text and cannot execute code.
Clicking a timed note seeks to that source-relative moment without rewriting trim bounds.
risks: Notes outside the selected interval still belong to the original source; the UI must make that context clear.
Deleting a note must never delete film.

tickets.title: Find film by search and combined football filters
tickets.outcome: Retrieve useful clips by what they show instead of browsing an expanding folder tree.
scope: Implement query, game, player, tag, phase, review-status, favorite, and archive filters.
Return totals and bounded pagination; show tag counts and library summary statistics.
non_goals: Semantic search, natural-language query agents, or automatic play classification.
acceptance_checks: Combining filters returns only records satisfying the documented intersection.
Default clip searches exclude archived clips while the explicit archived view can retrieve them.
Pagination returns stable pages with a total matching the same filters.
Empty searches and no-match searches display clear UI states.
Invalid identifiers/filter values return documented errors rather than leaking SQL details.
risks: Search meanings and ordering must be stable before saved filters are added.
Filter state must not imply AI labels have become accepted human tags.

tickets.title: Manage games and a simple manually maintained roster
tickets.outcome: Associate clips with the game and people the owner knows.
scope: Create and list games with opponent/date/season/notes.
Create and list player records with name, jersey, and position; associate clip metadata with these IDs.
non_goals: Automatic roster import, jersey OCR, face recognition, or treating per-play track IDs as roster IDs.
acceptance_checks: Game creation requires title and opponent and preserves optional fields.
Player creation preserves names, jerseys, and positions without treating jerseys as globally unique identities.
A clip can reference multiple existing players and an optional existing game.
Invalid relationship IDs cannot be saved.
The UI creates a game/player and then makes it available for clip assignment without restarting.
risks: Jersey numbers can repeat between teams and seasons; they are attributes, not primary keys.
The owner supplies roster identity in the first milestone.

tickets.title: Favorite and archive clips without losing film
tickets.outcome: Keep the active library focused while retaining earlier clips for later retrieval.
scope: Save favorite and archived flags through versioned metadata edits.
Expose quick favorite filters and an explicit archive view.
non_goals: Source deletion, disk cleanup, or inferring a coach's approval from a favorite.
acceptance_checks: Favoriting a clip updates the favorites filter and summary count.
Archiving removes the clip from the default active library but leaves its source and history intact.
Unarchiving restores the same clip ID and relationships.
Archived clips remain addressable and their playlist presentation is documented.
A stale favorite/archive update triggers the normal concurrency conflict rather than overwriting newer edits.
risks: Archive is a visibility choice, not a backup or deletion operation.
Derived statistics must use the documented active-clip population.

tickets.title: Create ordered playlists and watch a focused set of clips
tickets.outcome: Return to a useful sequence of plays without copying video files into more folders.
scope: Create playlists with title/description and replace ordered clip membership.
Display each playlist and play its clips in the saved order.
non_goals: Smart playlists, exported compilation movies, progress tracking, or per-viewer accounts.
acceptance_checks: Saving an ordered clip list and reopening it preserves order.
Unknown clip IDs and duplicate membership are rejected atomically.
Reordering does not duplicate or modify original media.
A playlist containing an archived clip has an explicit visible state rather than silently changing order.
The UI can create a playlist and watch more than one clip from it.
risks: Playlist membership references a clip whose trim may later change; version-frozen sessions are a later extension.
Empty playlists need a useful state.

tickets.title: Run durable audio-preserving trim exports
tickets.outcome: Produce a tightened MP4 that remains tied to the exact review settings used to create it.
scope: Queue exports from a frozen clip revision and retain job state/errors in SQLite.
Use bounded FFmpeg processing, optional source audio mapping, verified H.264 output, and atomic publication.
non_goals: Real-time transcoding, AI overlay rendering, task cancellation, or a distributed job queue.
acceptance_checks: A real generated fixture exports the selected duration within a declared codec tolerance and retains its audio stream.
A metadata edit made after enqueue does not change the queued export's interval or clip_version.
Source bytes remain unchanged and the completed job provides a valid download.
A nonzero process exit, missing executable, timeout, or write failure becomes a meaningful failed job.
Restart marks interrupted queued/running work failed according to the contract instead of announcing completion.
A partial output is never exposed as a completed artifact.
risks: Accurate trims re-encode; elapsed processing depends on source size and available encoders.
Do not silently drop audio as the inspected upstream overlay does.

tickets.title: Provide safe external Kinovea launch and KVA preservation
tickets.outcome: Keep Kinovea available for detailed technique review while retaining its sidecar with the library clip.
scope: Report configured Kinovea capability and launch only a locally configured executable on supported Windows systems.
Validate size-bounded KVA XML without DTD/entities, preserve original bytes, and download saved sidecars.
non_goals: Native Windows acceptance in this milestone, automatic working-zone/tag synchronization, or copying GPL code.
acceptance_checks: Unsupported platforms or missing configuration return an explicit unavailable reason.
A mocked Windows launch uses a command array and a managed clip path; request bodies cannot select an executable.
Malformed XML, DTD/entities, unsupported roots/schema, and oversized uploads are rejected.
A valid sidecar is preserved byte-for-byte and retrieved only through its clip association.
KVA import does not silently overwrite the library's tags, notes, trim, or source hash.
Documentation distinguishes adapter tests from the later real-Windows qualification gate.
risks: KVA schemas vary by release and may reference a different video/time origin.
Kinovea remains an external GPL v2 application; advanced mapping requires explicit compatibility work.

tickets.title: Import and review football-cv position suggestions safely
tickets.outcome: Attach external analysis to the right clip while keeping model suggestions distinct from coaching labels.
scope: Accept a revision-pinned position bundle with source SHA-256 and per-play tracking IDs.
Store immutable suggestion payloads and explicit unreviewed/accepted/rejected human review status.
non_goals: Running a detector, calibration UI, named-player recognition, or deriving play/technique tags from positions.
acceptance_checks: A valid position bundle is stored as unreviewed and lists its upstream revision.
A mismatched source SHA-256 is rejected without retaining a misleading analysis record.
Unsupported position tokens, malformed IDs, unknown schema fields, and non-finite data are rejected.
Changing review status preserves the imported payload and cannot affect another clip's record.
Accepting a suggestion does not assign roster players or populate human tags.
The UI identifies this as external analysis import and does not imply model execution is installed.
risks: Upstream results are uncertain and track IDs are scoped to a play/run.
The author's private-label benchmark is not a quality result for the owner's footage.

tickets.title: Deliver the complete same-origin local film-room interface
tickets.outcome: Complete the import, tighten, label, note, playlist, and export journey through one usable local interface.
scope: Build responsive clip browsing/review, metadata forms, management panels, upload progress, and pending-export polling.
Handle loading/empty/error states, stale selection responses, unsaved edits, and keyboard focus correctly.
non_goals: Native application packaging, remote hosted assets, automatic model analysis, or demo film presented as user data.
acceptance_checks: A new library starts empty and guides the owner to import clips.
The owner can import, select, trim, label, add a note, favorite, add to a playlist, and download an export.
Switching clip selection cannot show late data from a previous clip as the current record.
Typing in text inputs does not trigger playback shortcuts.
Server validation/conflict messages remain visible and unsaved edits are preserved or explicitly resolved.
User-controlled strings use safe DOM text rendering; scripts and styles load without a remote CDN.
risks: UI polish cannot substitute for a real end-to-end import/export test.
Different browser codecs and small displays require later expanded qualification.

tickets.title: Qualify source safety and the complete local media workflow
tickets.outcome: Establish evidence that core editing and export preserve the owner's film and reject unsafe requests.
scope: Run meaningful API/storage/security tests and one generated real-FFmpeg import-to-export workflow.
Check duplicate imports, concurrency, relationships, timestamps, range playback, safe paths, XML, and wrong-source analysis.
non_goals: Real model accuracy claims, live Windows Kinovea checks, or unsupported CI results reported as executed.
acceptance_checks: Generated test video with an audio tone proves import, persistence, selected export duration, audio retention, and unchanged source hash.
Negative tests exercise traversal/unsafe filenames, invalid relationships, stale edits, unsafe KVA, and wrong-source AI results.
Failure tests assert the actual returned error fields and durable job state.
The recorded qualification report distinguishes executed checks, failures, and environment-blocked gates.
No real game footage, model weights, credentials, or runtime database enters the commit.
risks: Passing unit tests alone does not establish decoder/encoder behavior.
Browser smoke is required when a local headless browser is available; otherwise record it unrun.

tickets.title: Package the first release and publish an honest handoff
tickets.outcome: Make the first working milestone installable and make its capabilities and remaining gates unambiguous.
scope: Build/install a wheel in an isolated environment, include static assets, and document startup/data location/dependencies.
Publish the ticket catalog, API contract, setup/user guidance, qualification evidence, and reviewable implementation PR.
non_goals: Auto-merge, native notarized installers, cloud deployment, or claiming every planned ticket is shipped.
acceptance_checks: A built wheel installs in isolation and serves its packaged UI assets.
The documented CLI and setup prerequisites match the actual package.
Formatter/linter and applicable test results are recorded with the tested revision/environment.
The complete ticket catalog validates without cycles, missing bodies, or nonexistent dependencies.
Implemented ticket statuses reference real evidence; GitHub issues remain open for PR review until merge.
README and handoff identify real CV inference, live Windows behavior, backup/restore, and advanced analysis as later work where unqualified.
risks: A source-tree run can hide missing wheel assets; installed-package verification is a separate gate.
User authorization covers pushing progress and opening a PR, not automatic merge.

tickets.title: Introduce reusable football tag groups and terminology
tickets.outcome: Apply consistent labels across games while allowing the owner to use their own football vocabulary.
scope: Add editable groups for phase, skill, formation, play concept, result, and review purpose with optional presets.
Support tag aliases/renames with explicit migration of existing associations and counts.
non_goals: Automatic tactical interpretation, a mandatory universal playbook, or changing accepted human labels without review.
acceptance_checks: A preset can apply a small useful tag set without requiring every metadata field.
An alias resolves to one canonical tag and avoids duplicate search results.
A rename previews affected clips and updates associations atomically.
Deleting a preset does not erase tags already applied to film.
Imported unfamiliar tags remain recoverable and can be mapped by the owner.
risks: Team terminology varies; rigid taxonomies can make a personal library slower to use.
Keep free-text tags compatible with the initial schema.

tickets.title: Apply batch metadata edits with preview and recovery
tickets.outcome: Label many clips from one game quickly without accidentally replacing unrelated review work.
scope: Add multi-select and batch game/player/tag/review actions with a concrete change preview.
Use per-clip versions, an auditable batch ID, and a recoverable before-state.
non_goals: Bulk source deletion or silently resolving concurrent edits.
acceptance_checks: Preview identifies affected clips and distinguishes add/remove/replace tag semantics.
A stale clip revision prevents that clip from being overwritten and produces an explicit conflict result.
The chosen all-or-nothing or partial-success policy is documented and tested.
Undo restores only fields changed by the batch and checks for subsequent edits.
A batch cannot assign nonexistent games/players or archive a clip outside the selected set.
risks: One unnoticed replacement can destroy many useful labels; batch intent must be visible.
Recovery must avoid overwriting changes made after the batch.

tickets.title: Support alternative cuts and multiple views of one source
tickets.outcome: Keep a wider analysis view and a tighter watching view without duplicating the original video.
scope: Separate immutable source assets from named selected intervals where the initial one-clip model requires it.
Allow several derived clip views with their own notes/tags while recording shared source ownership.
non_goals: Automatic full-game segmentation or joining unrelated source files.
acceptance_checks: Two named selections reference one physical source hash and independent start/end values.
Editing one view does not modify another view's trim or human labels.
Notes and exports identify both their source asset and selected view.
Existing first-release clips migrate without changed IDs or lost history.
The owner can select a wider context view for calibration while retaining the tight review view.
risks: Separating source assets and views is a schema evolution with backup requirements.
A hash match does not prove two records have identical intended editorial meaning.

tickets.title: Add accurate frame navigation and timeline previews
tickets.outcome: Move precisely around the snap, first step, and contact instead of repeatedly guessing timestamps.
scope: Generate a bounded frame/timestamp index and thumbnail strip tied to source media.
Support next/previous decoded-frame navigation and snapping in/out points to known timestamps.
non_goals: Claiming constant frame rate for every file or using browser currentTime alone as proof of frame accuracy.
acceptance_checks: A synthetic frame-numbered fixture confirms forward/back navigation targets the intended frame.
Variable-frame-rate input uses recorded presentation timestamps rather than frame/fps arithmetic.
Timeline thumbnails map to source-relative times and regenerate when their source hash differs.
Preview caches have documented disk bounds and never replace originals.
The UI explains any fallback to approximate browser seeking.
risks: Variable rates, rotation, and nonzero stream origins can misalign overlays.
Indexing cost should not block ordinary playback.

tickets.title: Qualify keyboard, accessibility, and small-screen review
tickets.outcome: Use the film room comfortably for repeated review sessions with a keyboard or a smaller display.
scope: Provide documented shortcuts, semantic form labels, focus management, and accessible status messages.
Refine responsive review/catalog layouts and large target sizes without obscuring video controls.
non_goals: A mobile-native app, remote synchronization, or changing clip metadata through ambiguous single-key shortcuts.
acceptance_checks: Keyboard-only navigation can import/select a clip, edit metadata, add a note, and export.
Shortcuts are inactive inside text-editing controls and dialogs return focus to their opener.
Errors, saving states, and job completion are announced without stealing focus.
Review tools remain usable at defined desktop and small-browser widths.
Contrast, labels, and focus checks are recorded against actual rendered pages.
risks: Automated accessibility scans do not establish usability for a full review session.
Playback shortcuts can conflict with browser defaults and text entry.

tickets.title: Compare two clips around explicit synchronization anchors
tickets.outcome: Compare repetitions or two camera angles at the moment that matters, such as the snap.
scope: Create comparison records referencing two clips and source-relative anchor timestamps.
Provide synchronized play/pause, adjustable offset, independent zoom, and a clear behavior at interval boundaries.
non_goals: Automatic temporal alignment, geometric camera fusion, or claiming calibrated measurements from arbitrary zoom.
acceptance_checks: Two generated videos with known offsets align within a declared playback tolerance.
Changing a comparison offset does not rewrite either source or clip trim.
Each panel identifies its game/clip and whether it shows original or derived media.
Pause/seek/speed controls behave consistently when one clip reaches its boundary.
Saved comparisons reopen with their selected clips, anchors, and layout.
risks: Different frame rates and browser decode load can introduce drift; state the measured tolerance.
Two views of one play need explicit linkage rather than filename inference.

tickets.title: Create source-anchored drawings and keyframe snapshots
tickets.outcome: Mark the foot placement, pursuit line, or player position that a future viewing should focus on.
scope: Add original-code arrows, circles, text, and simple freehand annotation with visibility intervals.
Store normalized geometry, source dimensions/time, and versioned snapshot exports.
non_goals: Copying Kinovea GPL drawing implementations, physical measurement claims, or automatic biomechanical coaching.
acceptance_checks: A drawing remains aligned when the player viewport is resized without changing the video coordinate system.
Visibility intervals and keyframes use original-source timestamps.
Undo/redo affects annotation revisions and never deletes source film.
Exported stills visibly include chosen annotations and retain source/time attribution in their manifest.
HTML/script-like annotation text is safely rendered and exported.
risks: Letterboxing, rotation, and cropped derivatives require explicit coordinate transforms.
Visible labels and hidden metadata notes are different outputs.

tickets.title: Save searches and maintain dynamic clip collections
tickets.outcome: Reopen a category such as tackling clips needing another look without rebuilding filters each time.
scope: Persist validated filter specifications as named saved searches.
Expose dynamic result counts/order and optional conversion to a fixed playlist snapshot.
non_goals: LLM-generated query execution, arbitrary SQL, or silently changing fixed playlist membership.
acceptance_checks: A saved search reuses the documented filter semantics after restart.
Newly labeled clips enter dynamic results while fixed playlists stay unchanged.
Unsupported filter versions are reported rather than ignored.
Converting results to a playlist preserves the reviewed order and selected clip IDs.
Renaming a tag through the taxonomy workflow has a documented effect on saved searches.
risks: Dynamic collections change over time; the UI must identify when a set is live versus frozen.
Queries must remain bounded at larger library sizes.

tickets.title: Add focused playlist review sessions and progress
tickets.outcome: Pick up a film session where the owner stopped and revisit the most useful plays.
scope: Persist a local session with playlist snapshot, clip position, replay count, and personal watch-again markers.
Provide next/previous, loop-current, review notes, and explicit finish/reset controls.
non_goals: Multi-user attendance analytics, notifications to other people, or grading players automatically.
acceptance_checks: A stopped session resumes at its stored clip and source-relative time after restart.
A subsequent playlist edit does not silently change a session's frozen order.
Replay counts and watch-again markers are local viewing metadata and do not change coaching approval.
The owner can reset progress without deleting clip notes or video.
Archived/missing references produce a recoverable state that preserves remaining order.
risks: Playback completion is not proof that the owner learned or approved a technique.
Frozen sessions require explicit choices when clips are edited.

tickets.title: Inspect supported KVA versions and propose metadata imports
tickets.outcome: Bring known Kinovea working-zone and keyframe information into the catalog with an explicit review step.
scope: Build release-specific KVA fixtures and a read-only normalized summary for recognized working-zone, keyframe, comment, and time-origin fields.
Present proposed catalog changes alongside the original preserved XML and unsupported elements.
non_goals: Arbitrary KVA schema compatibility, conversion of every drawing, or automatic writes back to Kinovea.
acceptance_checks: Fixtures from each declared supported release parse to expected source times and comments.
Unknown fields are retained in the original sidecar and reported as unsupported rather than discarded.
An import proposal identifies its sidecar hash, clip source hash, and KVA release/schema.
The owner must accept a preview before catalog trim or notes change.
Incorrect video associations or time-origin ambiguity block proposed timestamp updates.
risks: KVA time origins and import settings can change apparent timestamps.
A parseable XML file is not proof that every annotation is semantically understood.

tickets.title: Reconcile Kinovea and catalog edits without silent data loss
tickets.outcome: Return from external technique review with a clear account of what changed on both sides.
scope: Track last-imported sidecar hash and catalog revision; build a three-way comparison for supported fields.
Apply approved changes as new catalog revisions and preserve original/updated KVA versions.
non_goals: Bidirectional synchronization of unsupported fields, background sidecar overwrites, or direct changes to the user's original video.
acceptance_checks: Independent catalog and KVA edits to the same supported field produce an explicit conflict.
Unchanged fields do not generate duplicate notes or revisions on repeated imports.
Accepting a proposal records the KVA hash, reviewed changes, and prior/current clip versions.
Rejecting a proposal leaves both catalog and sidecar bytes intact.
Unknown KVA elements survive any documented sidecar export; otherwise export is disabled for that schema.
risks: Concurrent external saves can produce partially written sidecars; read atomically or ask for a saved file.
Timestamp mappings must be versioned and reversible.

tickets.title: Launch a Kinovea comparison from saved clip pairs
tickets.outcome: Open a selected pair for detailed external comparison with the correct film context.
scope: Extend the configured Windows launcher for documented second-video arguments and compatible per-clip sidecars.
Connect a saved comparison to the external handoff while preserving explicit unsupported states.
non_goals: A Kinovea replacement, DLL embedding, or assuming every installed version supports the same arguments.
acceptance_checks: Command construction passes both managed video paths as separate arguments and cannot accept request-supplied switches.
Capability checks distinguish single-video support from a version-qualified comparison launch.
The comparison record identifies both source hashes and chosen offsets even if Kinovea cannot import every setting.
Missing or moved executable/sidecars produce useful recovery instructions.
Real Windows launch acceptance is recorded under the Windows qualification ticket before claiming end-to-end support.
risks: The documented -video2 option does not establish an undocumented API for importing every catalog setting.
A comparison handoff must not lose the original source/analysis association.

tickets.title: Qualify a pinned external football-cv environment
tickets.outcome: Make optional analysis reproducible without adding heavy models to every film-room installation.
scope: Define an isolated external environment pinned to the reviewed football-cv revision and explicit dependency/model versions.
Record actual detector backend, device, weights provenance, licenses, cache location, and diagnostic health output.
non_goals: Bundling an unreviewed model, silently downloading weights at app startup, or claiming the README detector description matches code.
acceptance_checks: A declared environment records the football-cv commit and installed dependency versions.
Preflight reports the actual RF-DETR or torchvision backend and selected device, including unavailable reasons.
The stale ultralytics dependency guard is investigated with a documented upstream-compatible fix or an explicit requirement.
Any model acquisition is a separate deliberate setup operation with source/license/checksum recorded.
The base film library starts and remains usable with the entire CV environment absent.
risks: The pinned implementation differs from the README's YOLO description; environment behavior must be inspected directly.
Model code and weights have separate terms; the root Apache-2.0 license does not relicense them.

tickets.title: Create manual field calibration with validated geometry
tickets.outcome: Give the analyzer enough field context to place tracked participants in meaningful coordinates.
scope: Add a source-frame picker and editable pixel-to-field calibration points with units/field profile.
Store calibration revision, source hash, frame/timestamp, image dimensions, and provenance.
non_goals: Unreviewed automatic calibration or physical-accuracy claims from too few, collinear, or poorly distributed points.
acceptance_checks: At least four valid, spatially distributed correspondences are required before a calibration is runnable.
Non-finite, duplicate, out-of-image, and geometrically degenerate input receives a useful error.
Saving then reopening calibration preserves its source frame and coordinate/units convention.
The owner sees a projected grid/reprojection preview and can correct points before analysis.
Changing source geometry, crop, or orientation invalidates an incompatible calibration until reviewed.
risks: Wide field visibility and markings may be absent from tight clips.
Field profiles must make units and coordinate origin explicit instead of relying on undocumented assumptions.

tickets.title: Review analysis suitability and pre-snap context
tickets.outcome: Avoid spending analysis time on clips that cannot support reliable alignment-based positions.
scope: Add a preflight checklist backed by actual clip properties and owner-selected snap/context timestamps.
Record offense direction, team-color/role review, camera cuts, crop context, and reasons for unsuitable clips.
non_goals: Automatic play recognition, assuming the ball is visible, or presenting a model snap estimate as ground truth.
acceptance_checks: A clip with missing calibration or insufficient pre-snap context is marked needs_input with a clear next action.
Manual snap selection uses the source timestamp/frame mapping and is persisted in the run request.
Team/direction assignments are explicit reviewed inputs or labeled suggestions.
A detected or manually marked camera cut prevents treating incompatible calibration as continuous.
The owner can still catalog/watch an unsuitable clip with analysis disabled.
risks: Very short highlights may omit the alignment that drives position classification.
Camera movement and jersey-color similarity can degrade geometry and team assignment.

tickets.title: Execute bounded, resumable external analysis jobs
tickets.outcome: Run an optional analysis without freezing review or losing the record of what was processed.
scope: Supervise the configured external Python process using persistent per-run directories and stable play IDs.
Snapshot inputs, log bounded stage progress, support cancel/retry, and retain terminal failure reasons.
non_goals: Shell-command input, arbitrary filesystem/executable selection, or silently resuming with changed source/calibration/model inputs.
acceptance_checks: A run snapshot records source hash, trim/context, calibration revision, provider commit, detector/weights, and command version.
Process invocation uses argument arrays, managed paths, time/resource limits, and explicit local-only inputs.
Cancellation terminates owned processes and never advertises partial results as successful.
A retry creates a new attempt while preserving previous errors and artifacts.
Restart recovery distinguishes interrupted, retryable, failed, and complete work.
A deterministic fake runner qualifies supervision independently from later real-model accuracy tests.
risks: The upstream analyze API defaults to temporary storage unless a persistent directory is supplied.
A stuck detector or insufficient GPU memory must not corrupt the library.

tickets.title: Import full analysis artifacts with a versioned manifest
tickets.outcome: Inspect how positions were produced and rebuild overlays without losing intermediate evidence.
scope: Extend the position-only adapter with schemas for detections, tracks, teams, field coordinates, snap, and labels.
Ingest a manifest with hashes, timebase, transform chain, and links to each immutable per-run artifact.
non_goals: Accepting arbitrary pickle/model objects, trusting archive paths, or treating partial output as complete analysis.
acceptance_checks: Fixture bundles from the pinned revision validate against explicit adapter schema versions.
Every referenced file exists, matches its recorded checksum, and remains inside its managed run directory.
Frame indices/timestamps and box coordinates are checked against the declared source/proxy transform.
Missing, malformed, oversized, or wrong-source artifacts block final acceptance with precise diagnostics.
Position-only imports remain compatible and clearly lack richer track/render capability.
risks: Upstream stage formats can change without the public README changing.
Intermediate JSON may be large; limits and streaming/paging decisions need measured fixtures.

tickets.title: Render reviewed position overlays with source audio and timing
tickets.outcome: Watch useful player-position boxes while retaining the sound and provenance of the original play.
scope: Render optional overlays from validated tracking artifacts and accepted correction layers.
Preserve source audio according to a documented mapping policy and keep original/overlay playback separately available.
non_goals: Replacing source footage, silently baking unreviewed names into video, or copying the upstream renderer unchanged.
acceptance_checks: A generated motion fixture verifies box placement, label timing, output duration, and preserved audio.
Rendered files cite source hash, run ID, reviewed label revision, and render settings.
The owner can switch between clean film and the derived overlay without losing the playback moment.
Failed renders leave no completed artifact and can be rerun from preserved intermediates.
Unknown/low-quality tracks can be hidden without deleting the raw analysis.
Different source frame rates and proxy transforms are qualified before being declared supported.
risks: The inspected upstream overlay loses source audio and rebuilds time from OpenCV frame rate.
Variable-frame-rate footage requires timestamp-aware rendering.

tickets.title: Correct suggested positions through a human review ledger
tickets.outcome: Fix an incorrect linebacker or quarterback suggestion without erasing what the model originally said.
scope: Provide per-track position correction, rejection/suppression, rationale, and revision history.
Keep provider output immutable and expose effective reviewed labels as a separate projection.
non_goals: Training a model automatically, changing the source suggestion payload, or equating accepted position with named roster identity.
acceptance_checks: Changing a track's position records old suggestion, chosen label, source/run/track IDs, and review time.
Rejecting a suggestion leaves its original payload available for comparison.
Only supported position tokens or an explicit unknown/suppressed state can become effective labels.
An older run's correction is not applied to a new run merely because a numeric track ID repeats.
Exports and overlays state whether their labels are unreviewed suggestions or human-reviewed values.
risks: Track IDs are scoped to a run and can change on reprocessing.
A correction UI must preserve uncertainty rather than requiring a guessed position.

tickets.title: Link tracks to roster players through explicit scoped review
tickets.outcome: Find a known player's appearances while keeping identity decisions separate from geometry-based role predictions.
scope: Add manual mapping from run/clip/track/time interval to a roster record with evidence notes.
Support unknown identity, correction, revocation, and history without automatic cross-game propagation.
non_goals: Face recognition, automatic persistent biometric identity, or treating a jersey number as globally unique.
acceptance_checks: A reviewed mapping includes clip ID, run ID, track ID, interval, roster ID, and decision provenance.
Repeated track IDs in another clip/run have no identity effect.
Revoking or changing a mapping updates derived player views without rewriting historical decisions.
Ambiguous/occluded tracks can remain unassigned.
Player-filter results distinguish manual clip tags from specifically reviewed track identity.
risks: A stitched track may accidentally include two people; interval-scoped review must allow correction.
Jerseys and positions can change between games.

tickets.title: Evaluate position quality on representative owner film
tickets.outcome: Know which analysis suggestions are useful for this footage and where the owner must review closely.
scope: Create an authorized local evaluation set with varied games, views, lighting, and positions, plus human labels.
Measure per-class confusion, coverage, track quality, calibration error where available, runtime, and failure reasons.
non_goals: Committing private game footage, transferring benchmark percentages from another dataset, or declaring success from a single attractive overlay.
acceptance_checks: Evaluation records source hashes and annotation policy while keeping actual private film outside git.
Train/tune/evaluate splits keep plays and related frames separated to prevent leakage.
Results include class counts, unknown/unlabeled cases, and errors as well as aggregate metrics.
The report compares unreviewed suggestions to reviewed labels and states uncertainty/sample limitations.
Only supported footage profiles are enabled as qualified; unsupported cases remain review-first.
A reproducible command and environment manifest permit rerunning the evaluation.
risks: The upstream roughly 70% result uses 21 private-labeled plays and is not an acceptance threshold for this project.
Small class populations can make apparently good percentages unstable.

tickets.title: Transfer calibration between compatible plays with review
tickets.outcome: Reduce repeated field-point marking when clips share a usable camera setup.
scope: Attempt upstream-compatible calibration transfer from an explicitly selected same-game reference.
Record reference/target hashes, transform quality, candidate points, and a manual accept/edit/reject decision.
non_goals: Blind reuse across games/camera angles or overwriting an existing manual calibration.
acceptance_checks: A accepted transfer records its reference calibration revision and target source hash.
A target with incompatible geometry or inadequate matching is marked failed/needs_review.
Existing manual calibration is never replaced without an explicit reviewed change.
A visual grid/reprojection preview exposes a bad transfer before position processing.
Qualified and deliberately mismatched test pairs demonstrate the rejection path.
risks: The same game does not guarantee an unchanged camera or crop.
Feature matches can look plausible while producing wrong field geometry.

tickets.title: Detect and review tracking gaps and identity switches
tickets.outcome: Prevent a convincing overlay from following the wrong player after a collision or occlusion.
scope: Add track-quality flags for impossible jumps, long gaps, fragmented paths, edge exits, and conflicting overlaps.
Provide reviewed suppress/split/link suggestions with provenance and invalidate affected downstream views.
non_goals: Claiming perfect multi-object tracking, automatic cross-camera identity, or modifying provider artifacts in place.
acceptance_checks: Synthetic track fixtures expose known gaps and swaps with reproducible diagnostics.
A manual split/link decision is scoped to source/run/time and preserves original tracks.
Changing track continuity marks dependent position/identity/render decisions stale until reviewed.
Low-quality tracks remain visible as uncertain or can be hidden without pretending they were never detected.
The real-film evaluation records examples where stitching improves or harms results.
risks: Occlusion can make the correct answer unknowable from one view.
Tracking-quality scores must be calibrated before thresholds become automatic decisions.

tickets.title: Package a convenient macOS local launcher
tickets.outcome: Open the film library on the owner's Mac without reconstructing a development environment for every session.
scope: Provide a documented local launcher/bundle that opens the same-origin UI and uses a stable user-data location.
Qualify Intel/Apple Silicon targets actually available, external FFmpeg setup, process ownership, and clean shutdown.
non_goals: Claiming Kinovea runs on Apple Silicon, bundling heavy CV models, or claiming notarization/signing that was not performed.
acceptance_checks: A clean supported Mac can install/start the documented package and reopen the same persisted library.
Launching twice focuses/reuses or cleanly rejects the second instance instead of starting competing workers.
Paths with spaces and Unicode work for uploads, data, and export downloads.
Missing FFmpeg and unavailable Kinovea are visible with useful setup guidance.
The release matrix records hardware, OS, signing status, and executed checks separately for each tested architecture.
risks: macOS browser review and Kinovea support are separate capabilities.
Packaging Python and codec executables requires update and licensing discipline.

tickets.title: Qualify Windows packaging and live Kinovea workflows
tickets.outcome: Use the film room and Kinovea together on a real supported Windows installation.
scope: Package or document a repeatable Windows installation and configured external Kinovea path.
Execute live single/comparison launch, saved sidecar reopening, field mapping, and Unicode/space path checks.
non_goals: Emulating native acceptance through mocks, redistributing Kinovea source inside this repository, or assuming every old release behaves identically.
acceptance_checks: The test record names Windows, CPU architecture, Kinovea release, Python/runtime, and FFmpeg versions.
A managed source opens in the configured Kinovea application and a saved KVA can be preserved/reopened.
The -video2 comparison handoff is tested on the declared supported release.
Unsupported KVA versions and unavailable executables fail clearly without changing the catalog.
Core import/trim/export retains audio and source hash on Windows.
Installer/launcher uninstall leaves user media and the database intact.
risks: Command-line quoting and file locks behave differently on Windows.
Success with one Kinovea version does not qualify every version.

tickets.title: Back up and restore a complete film library
tickets.outcome: Recover the owner's clips, labels, sidecars, and review history on a replacement computer.
scope: Create a consistent SQLite backup plus a versioned manifest for sources, derived files, notes, revisions, playlists, KVA, and analysis records.
Restore into a new managed workspace with checksum verification and a dry-run report.
non_goals: Automatic cloud upload, treating a database-only copy as a complete backup, or overwriting a live library without explicit reviewed intent.
acceptance_checks: Backup taken while the app is active contains a consistent database snapshot and an explicit policy for in-flight jobs.
Restore into an empty workspace preserves IDs, relationships, source hashes, history, and playlists.
Missing/corrupt manifest files are reported before the restore is activated.
Untrusted archive paths, symlinks, and oversized members cannot escape the destination.
The process is resumable or safely restartable and never deletes originals to make room.
A documented recovery drill opens restored clips and exports a verified audio-preserving trim.
risks: Derived caches can be regenerated, but original film and reviewed decisions must be included or explicitly identified as missing.
File-by-file copying of an actively written database is not a sufficient consistency strategy.

tickets.title: Export portable metadata and selected film packages
tickets.outcome: Carry organized review work into another application or share a selected set as files.
scope: Export stable JSON/CSV metadata and a selected clip/playlist package with provenance manifests.
Include optional trimmed MP4s, notes, and preserved sidecars under deterministic safe filenames.
non_goals: Sending files to other people automatically, public links, or presenting editable KVA metadata as burned-in video text.
acceptance_checks: A package identifies source clip/hash, selected interval, label revision, playlist order, and included files.
Metadata preserves Unicode, multiple tags/players, and null/optional values without ambiguity.
CSV output escapes delimiters/newlines and handles spreadsheet-formula injection safely.
The owner can export metadata without copying original or derived videos.
Package inspection/import validates checksums/schema and does not run executable content.
A selected package contains only the requested clips and associated records.
risks: CSV cannot naturally represent every nested relationship; JSON is the canonical round-trip form.
Annotation comments remain metadata unless an explicit render/export operation makes them visible.

tickets.title: Harden database migration and interrupted-write recovery
tickets.outcome: Upgrade the application or recover from disk problems without losing a usable library.
scope: Introduce versioned, reversible-where-feasible migrations and backup-before-upgrade checks.
Handle disk-full, database lock, interrupted copy, and interrupted publication paths with explicit recovery state.
non_goals: Silently repairing unknown corruption, downgrading incompatible schemas, or deleting film to free space.
acceptance_checks: Migrating a prior-version fixture preserves clip IDs, source hashes, revisions, and relationships.
An interrupted migration rolls back or leaves a documented recoverable backup; partial schema is not opened as healthy.
A newer unsupported database version is rejected with recovery guidance.
Injected disk-full and permission failures do not mark media/artifacts complete.
Startup identifies missing sources/orphan partial outputs without treating them as normal clips.
Recovery procedures are demonstrated on copied fixtures rather than the only copy of user film.
risks: Database atomicity does not by itself make filesystem writes atomic.
Reversible migration depends on retaining old data and backups.

tickets.title: Show storage health and safely reclaim derived caches
tickets.outcome: Understand disk use and remove reproducible previews/exports without risking original game film.
scope: Report storage use by originals, thumbnails, exports, analysis artifacts, temporary files, and backups.
Offer a concrete selection/preview for deleting regenerable caches and completed export copies, with reference checks.
non_goals: Original-source deletion, removing the only copy of a reviewed sidecar, or assuming archive means safe to erase.
acceptance_checks: Storage totals identify the managed paths and artifact types being counted.
Cleanup preview states which files will be removed and whether each can be regenerated.
Running jobs, active downloads, and required provenance artifacts are excluded or safely coordinated.
Cleanup rejects paths outside the managed workspace and refuses original media.
Deleting a thumbnail/export leaves clip metadata, source film, review history, and playlists usable.
Failed deletions report remaining files rather than claiming all space was recovered.
risks: Analysis outputs may be expensive or impossible to recreate with a missing old model; classify retention carefully.
Backups may depend on files that look like duplicates.

tickets.title: Qualify larger libraries and a representative media matrix
tickets.outcome: Keep film retrieval and playback useful after a season of clips and varied camera formats.
scope: Benchmark a synthetic catalog with 10,000 clips and realistic many-to-many labels/playlists.
Test declared codecs, resolutions, frame rates, orientation metadata, silent/audio sources, and slow/damaged files.
non_goals: Universal codec guarantees, invented hardware performance, or repeated optional tests after a stated gate is satisfied.
acceptance_checks: On the recorded reference machine, paginated common filters over 10,000 metadata records meet a documented 500 ms p95 target or remain unqualified.
Browser browsing remains bounded rather than loading every full clip/media resource at once.
The supported media matrix records import, preview, range playback, exact export, and audio outcomes separately.
Unsupported formats receive actionable messages instead of a successful-looking broken thumbnail.
Large imports/exports do not starve metadata editing and job state remains truthful.
Benchmarks include schema/index/query details sufficient to reproduce observed limits.
risks: Metadata query latency and media decode latency are different measurements.
High-resolution or variable-frame-rate footage may need an explicit proxy policy.

tickets.title: Maintain dependency provenance and upstream upgrade gates
tickets.outcome: Keep integrations reproducible and avoid breaking the film library when dependencies or external projects change.
scope: Record a dependency inventory, lock strategy, license notices, external model sources, and pinned adapter compatibility.
Create an update checklist that reviews upstream changes, schema fixtures, and affected qualified workflows.
non_goals: Relicensing upstream code, claiming one root license covers model weights, or copying unlicensed alternatives.
acceptance_checks: The repository retains Apache-2.0 for original code and documents separately governed external tools/dependencies.
football-cv code commit, backend versions, and weight artifacts are independently identifiable.
Updating an adapter pin requires fixture/schema regression checks and a reviewed capability change note.
Kinovea stays external and GPL/AGPL alternatives are referenced without source ingestion.
A release inventory distinguishes distributed dependencies from optional user-installed tools.
The policy provides a safe rollback pin and does not auto-update analysis components at app startup.
risks: A license declaration in a README does not establish the terms of every bundled asset.
README/code drift is already observed in football-cv's detector.

tickets.title: Run a complete owner-workflow release qualification
tickets.outcome: Deliver a release the owner can trust for repeated real film review, with remaining limits explicitly recorded.
scope: Execute the import/tighten/label/retrieve/review/compare/playlist/export/backup/restore journey on each declared platform.
Publish the capability matrix, installation/recovery guide, test evidence, open defects, and rollback instructions.
non_goals: Declaring optional CV qualified without representative evaluation, closing tickets solely because code exists, or auto-merging without authorization.
acceptance_checks: Every claimed feature maps to a ticket, code revision, environment, and executed acceptance evidence.
A representative owner-approved film workflow completes without altered source hashes or lost review decisions.
A backup/restore drill demonstrates retrieval and export after migration to a clean workspace.
Windows Kinovea and each CV environment are labeled qualified, unsupported, or unrun separately from browser functionality.
Any open release-blocking issue prevents the corresponding support claim.
Release notes distinguish implemented candidates, locally verified behavior, merged completion, and planned expansion.
risks: A single green environment does not qualify every operating system or camera setup.
Full qualification may deliberately ship a limited capability matrix if optional analysis remains experimental.
